name: Charles McDew
bio: Charles McDew was chairman of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee. He was first jailed in 1960 leading the Orangeburg, South Carolina sit-ins, and on Oct. 4, 1961 was arrested again on the courthouse steps in McComb, Mississippi during the student walkout supporting the SNCC voter-registration drive.
charges: Breach of peace / sit-in and demonstration arrests
sentence: Jailed for civil-rights sit-ins and demonstrations

name: Thomas Gaither
bio: Thomas Gaither was a field secretary of the Congress of Racial Equality who, with eight Rock Hill, South Carolina students, was sentenced to 30 days on a chain gang for a lunch-counter sit-in at a McCrory's store in early 1961 — refusing the alternative fine in the influential 'jail, no bail' protest.
charges: Trespass / breach of peace — Rock Hill lunch-counter sit-in
convicted: Convicted; chose the chain gang over a fine (1961)

name: Frank Stanley
bio: Frank Stanley was a Louisville integration leader (an assistant to the publisher of the Louisville Defender) jailed on March 14, 1961 in the mass arrests of more than 260 demonstrators during the downtown-desegregation sit-ins and stand-ins.
sentence: Jailed in the Louisville desegregation arrests

name: W. J. Hodge
bio: The Rev. W. J. Hodge, president of the Louisville NAACP, was jailed in the March 14, 1961 mass arrest of downtown-desegregation demonstrators in Louisville.
sentence: Jailed in the Louisville desegregation arrests

name: F. G. Sampson
bio: The Rev. F. G. Sampson, vice-president of the Louisville NAACP, was jailed with other leaders in the March 14, 1961 mass arrest of desegregation demonstrators in downtown Louisville.
sentence: Jailed in the Louisville desegregation arrests

name: Barbara A. Thomas
bio: Barbara A. Thomas was a 21-year-old student at the Virginia Theological Seminary and College who served a 30-day jail term in Lynchburg in 1961 for a drugstore lunch-counter sit-in. She was also a lead petitioner in a suit challenging federal grants to segregated institutions.

name: Mark Lane
bio: Mark Lane was a New York State Assemblyman who joined the 1961 Freedom Rides and was arrested on an integrated bus ride and jailed in Jackson, Mississippi. He was sentenced to four months (two suspended) and a $200 fine for 'breach of the peace,' and appealed.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation
sentence: Four months (two suspended) and a $200 fine

name: Percy Sutton
bio: Percy Sutton, president of the Manhattan branch of the NAACP, was arrested with Mark Lane as a 1961 Freedom Rider testing bus desegregation and jailed in Jackson, Mississippi, drawing the same four-month sentence (two suspended) and $200 fine for 'breach of the peace.'
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation
sentence: Four months (two suspended) and a $200 fine

name: James Farmer
bio: James Farmer was the national director of the Congress of Racial Equality and the principal organizer of the 1961 Freedom Rides. Arrested as a Freedom Rider in Jackson, Mississippi, he served 39 days in jail — moved from the Jackson city jail to the Hinds County jail to the Parchman state penitentiary — and acted as spokesman for the jailed riders.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation

name: Price Chatham
bio: Price Chatham was a Freedom Rider from East Rockaway, Long Island, jailed in Mississippi and held at the Parchman state penitentiary, where he carried on a hunger strike of more than three weeks protesting the segregation of Black and white riders within the prison.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation
sentence: Jailed at Parchman; hunger strike against prison segregation

name: John Collier
bio: John Collier was one of a group of clergymen who rode as Freedom Riders to test segregated facilities in Florida in June 1961 and were arrested after a sit-in at the Tallahassee airport restaurant.
charges: Breach of peace / trespass — Tallahassee airport Freedom Ride
sentence: Arrested testing travel desegregation; released on bond

name: Arthur Hardge
bio: Arthur Hardge was among the interfaith group of Freedom Riders arrested at the Tallahassee airport in June 1961 while testing the desegregation of travel facilities in Florida.
charges: Breach of peace / trespass — Tallahassee airport Freedom Ride
sentence: Arrested testing travel desegregation; released on bond

name: Miriam Feingold
bio: Miriam Feingold was a 20-year-old Swarthmore College student from Brooklyn who rode as a Freedom Rider in 1961 and spent 31 days in Mississippi jails — five at the Hinds County jail in Jackson and the rest at the Parchman state penitentiary — for testing interstate desegregation.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation

name: Felix Singer
bio: Felix Singer was a 32-year-old Freedom Rider from Chicago jailed at the Parchman state penitentiary in Mississippi in 1961. For their total passive resistance he and Terry Sullivan were dragged naked across concrete floors with 'wrist breakers' and shocked with electric cattle prods.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation
sentence: Jailed at Parchman; tortured for passive resistance

name: Terry Sullivan
bio: Terry Sullivan was a 19-year-old Freedom Rider from Chicago jailed at the Parchman state penitentiary in 1961. With Felix Singer he was subjected to 'wrist breakers' and electric cattle prods for refusing to cooperate with the segregated prison.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing interstate desegregation
sentence: Jailed at Parchman; tortured for passive resistance

name: Robert Jenkins
bio: Robert Jenkins was the chairman of St. Louis CORE who was arrested in June 1961 as a Freedom Rider testing the airport facilities in Jackson, Mississippi. He was later acquitted of the breach-of-peace charge on a technicality.
charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride testing airport desegregation

name: Wyatt T. Walker
bio: The Rev. Wyatt Tee Walker, executive director of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, was one of four Negro leaders arrested in Montgomery, Alabama on May 25, 1961 for 'breaching the peace' during the Freedom Ride crisis.
charges: Breach of the peace — Montgomery (Freedom Ride crisis)
sentence: Arrested in the Montgomery Freedom Ride arrests

name: Bernard Lee
bio: Bernard Lee was a student civil-rights activist (earlier expelled from Alabama State College for a 1960 sit-in) who was among the four Negro leaders arrested in Montgomery on May 25, 1961 for 'breaching the peace' during the Freedom Rides.
charges: Breach of the peace — Montgomery (Freedom Ride crisis)
sentence: Arrested in the Montgomery Freedom Ride arrests
